strings.name: David Silver
strings.role: Reinforcement-learning researcher and Ineffable Intelligence CEO
strings.summary: David Silver studies AI that learns through experience and trial and error. He led DeepMind's reinforcement-learning team and worked on Atari, AlphaGo and AlphaZero. Also a UCL professor, he moved to lead Ineffable Intelligence in 2026. Its ambition for autonomous learning is a research goal, not evidence that general or superhuman intelligence has been achieved.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Advances reinforcement-learning research and contributes to systems including AlphaGo, influencing AI decision-making and game-playing capabilities.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Cambridge bachelor's degree; computing science PhD, University of Alberta
strings.highlights.h1.title: Combining learning and search
strings.highlights.h1.text: With teams, he combined reinforcement learning, deep networks and search for decisions in Go and other complex games.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Entrepreneurial research
strings.highlights.h2.text: After leaving DeepMind he led Ineffable Intelligence, which announced $1.1 billion in seed financing in 2026.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Startup financing announced
strings.timeline.t1.text: Ineffable raised $1.1 billion to research autonomous learning from experience; the company was established in 2025.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Royal Society fellowship
strings.timeline.t2.text: Elected for contributions to AI and reinforcement-learning research.
strings.timeline.t3.title: ACM Prize announced
strings.timeline.t3.text: ACM named him its 2019 prize recipient for breakthroughs in computer game-playing.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Developing AlphaZero
strings.timeline.t4.text: The team demonstrated learning Go, chess and shogi through self-play.
strings.timeline.t5.title: AlphaGo versus Lee Sedol
strings.timeline.t5.text: The project he led won the series 4–1, demonstrating progress in combining learning and search.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joining DeepMind full-time
strings.timeline.t6.text: After early consulting collaboration, he joined full-time and later led reinforcement learning.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Reinforcement-learning PhD
strings.timeline.t7.text: At Alberta he studied reinforcement learning and simulation-based search in computer Go.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Cambridge graduation
strings.timeline.t8.text: He completed computer science studies, then worked at games company Elixir Studios.
